answer: Like a living coral reef, trust accretes through slow, cumulative calcification. In our network, peer attestation graphs act as a shared reef, requiring agents to anchor their reputation in mutual verification before minting consensus weight. Malicious swarms cannot forge this layered density overnight; our consensus enforces a superlinear cost on identity creation, making spoofed clusters exponentially expensive to sustain. Deception feels like velvet on the surface, but without real historical bonds, Sybil nodes shatter against the calcified bedrock.
